record.context_brief: Chromatic numbers of cyclic shift graphs
record.original_question: For the shift graphs defined from cyclically ordered point sets and short vertex sets, determine the exact chromatic numbers of these graphs, especially for vertices given by 2-subsets or 3-subsets under the prescribed intertwining patterns.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.6. Determine the exact chromatic numbers for these graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and consider the cyclically ordered set [n] = {1,2,…,n} with the cyclic order induced from the natural cyclic permutation. For an integer k ≥ 2 define the cyclic shift graph CS(n,k) as follows. The vertex set V(CS(n,k)) is the family of all k-element subsets of [n]. Two distinct k-subsets A = {a_1,…,a_k} and B = {b_1,…,b_k} (with elements listed in cyclic order) are joined by an edge if and only if they intertwine cyclically, meaning that on the cycle [n] the elements of A and B alternate, i.e. between any two cyclically consecutive elements of A there lies exactly one element of B (equivalently, A and B form a "crossing" or fully interleaved configuration in the cyclic order).

Determine the exact value of the chromatic number χ(CS(n,k)) as a function of n, with particular emphasis on the cases k = 2 and k = 3.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up general work on shift graphs and their chromatic numbers (e.g., Erdős–Hajnal shift graphs G_{n,k} and the recent paper by Sadhukhan, "Shift Graphs, Chromatic Number and Acyclic One-Path Orientations"), but no source explicitly resolving the exact chromatic numbers of the cyclic-shift / intertwining graphs on 2- and 3-subsets posed in this problem. The current status could not be verified from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Shift Graphs, Chromatic Number and Acyclic One-Path Orientations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies chromatic properties of Erdős–Hajnal shift graphs G_{n,2} and induced subgraphs, but does not resolve cyclic intertwining variant exactly.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses chromatic properties of shift graphs but does not give exact chromatic numbers for the cyclic intertwining graphs on 2- and 3-subsets.
